study: Kutaka et al. 2017, Primarily Math elementary math specialist program (J. Teacher Education)
eval_evidence: Authored by the Primarily Math research team at UNL; several original-grant PIs are senior authors and the program's architects (p.143). Lead author/RAs were not the original architects, but the developers co-authored and ran the evaluation.
developer_evidence: PD = six graduate-level university courses / summer institutes delivered by the Primarily Math program (university faculty who designed it); 'lead author and graduate research assistants ... sometimes helped deliver the PD' (p.142-143).
cascade_evidence: Program faculty/research team teach the graduate coursework and institutes directly to participating teachers; no train-the-trainer/lead-teacher intermediary layer described.
counterfactual_evidence: Comparison group = teachers in matched non-participating buildings with no Primarily Math, matched on building FRL%, enrollment, racial composition; received no alternative PD (p.144, comparison-group para).
coaching_evidence: PD is coursework-based (6 grad courses over 13 months, 2 summer institutes); no ongoing in-class coaching/observation cycles described in the logic model or methods.
student_dose_evidence: Intervention changes the teacher's own mathematics instruction only; no tutoring, pull-out, extra minutes, or student software dose. TEMA-3 'pull-out' was assessment only.
maturity_evidence: 4-year multi-cohort longitudinal design; student-achievement HLM pools fall-spring growth across measurement occasions 2009-2013 (Table 3, Fig 2), with effects largest in years 2-3 of teacher participation; not restricted to the first implementation year.
